I farm only 6.5 mu, and I do it alone at 72, so I will keep the full wheat-maize rotation on all of my land because it is the system I know best and it matches my well irrigation. I am educated and have farmed for 50 years, so I do not need to gamble on complicated changes. I will use better seed on both crops to keep yield stable, but I will manage inputs conservatively because my land is small and I care more about reliable output than chasing the very highest yield. For wheat, I will use improved seed, apply moderate nitrogen with enough phosphorus and some potassium, irrigate three times through the season, and use rotary tillage because it is efficient for me and fits my labor capacity. For maize, I will plant hybrid seed after wheat harvest, keep fertilizer at a moderate level, irrigate twice with my well if rainfall is not enough, and continue rotary tillage to save time and effort. I will keep pesticide use limited but timely, because on a small farm I can watch fields closely and respond when needed. My goal this year is steady production, manageable labor, and low risk.
